title: Roast Chicken
intro: A whole bird roasted on a bed of onion and carrot, with lemon, garlic and thyme butter keeping the meat juicy under crisp golden skin.
ingredients: 1 whole head of garlic, halved crossways
Small bunch fresh thyme, leaves picked from half
200 ml (¾ cup) chicken stock or water, for the pan gravy
steps: Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking and pat it dry all over with kitchen paper. Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F, fan 180 °C).

Mash the butter with the picked thyme leaves, the lemon zest, ½ teaspoon salt and plenty of black pepper. Loosen the skin over the breasts with your fingers and push about half of the butter underneath, then smear the rest over the outside of the bird.
Tuck the lemon halves, the garlic halves and the rosemary into the cavity along with the remaining thyme sprigs. Tie the legs together with kitchen string so the bird holds its shape.
Scatter the onion and carrot over the base of a roasting tin about 30 x 25 cm (12 x 10 in), toss with the oil and sit the chicken on top, breast up. Season the skin generously with salt.

Roast for 1 hour 20 to 1 hour 30 minutes, basting with the pan juices once or twice. It is done when the juices run clear from the thickest part of the thigh and a thermometer there reads 75 °C (165 °F). If the skin darkens too quickly, cover loosely with foil.
Lift the chicken onto a board, tent loosely with foil and leave to rest for 15 to 20 minutes before carving.

While it rests, set the roasting tin over medium heat, pour in the stock and scrape up the sticky bits. Squeeze the soft roasted garlic and lemon from the cavity into the tin, bubble for 3 to 4 minutes, then strain into a jug and serve alongside the carved chicken.

title: Chicken Pot Pie
intro: Chunks of chicken and sweet vegetables in a thick, herby cream sauce under a puffed golden pastry lid.
ingredients: 500 g (1 lb 2 oz) cooked chicken, torn into bite-sized pieces
1 sheet ready-rolled puff pastry, about 320 g (11 oz)
steps: If you are starting from raw chicken, poach 3 skinless breasts in gently simmering stock for 15 to 18 minutes until cooked through, then cool and tear into pieces, keeping the stock for the sauce.
Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 8 to 10 minutes until softened but not browned.

Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the stock a little at a time, stirring so no lumps form, then add the milk. Simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Stir in the chicken, peas, thyme and parsley and season well. Let the filling cool for 10 minutes, then spoon it into a 23 cm (9 in) pie dish or a 1.5 litre (6 cup) baking dish.

Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F, fan 180 °C). Lay the pastry over the dish, trim the overhang, press the edges down against the rim and cut two or three slits in the top so steam can escape. Brush all over with beaten egg.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the pastry is risen and deep golden and the filling is bubbling at the edges. Leave to stand for 10 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup
intro: A clear, golden chicken broth full of shredded meat, soft vegetables and tender egg noodles.
ingredients: 600 g (1 lb 5 oz) bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs
Squeeze of lemon juice, to finish
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6 to 8 minutes until they begin to soften. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.

Pour in the stock and add the chicken thighs, bay leaves and thyme. Bring to the boil, skim off any foam, then lower the heat and simmer gently, partly covered, for 30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift the chicken out onto a plate. Once cool enough to handle, discard the skin and bones and shred the meat with two forks.
Bring the broth back to a steady simmer, add the noodles and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, or as the packet directs, until tender.

Return the shredded chicken to the pot and warm through for 2 minutes. Fish out the bay leaves, season to taste with salt and pepper, and finish with the parsley and a squeeze of lemon before ladling into bowls.

title: Grilled Salmon
intro: Crisp-skinned salmon fillets with a lemon, garlic and dill rub, grilled alongside charred asparagus spears.
ingredients: 4 salmon fillets, skin on, about 170 g (6 oz) each
400 g (14 oz) asparagus, woody ends snapped off
1 lemon, zested, then cut into wedges
steps: Heat a barbecue or a ridged grill pan to medium-high, about 200 °C (400 °F), and brush the grates with a little oil. Pat the salmon dry with kitchen paper.

Stir 2 tablespoons of the oil with the garlic, lemon zest, dill, ½ teaspoon salt and some pepper, and rub it over the flesh side of the salmon. Toss the asparagus with the remaining oil, salt and pepper.

Lay the salmon skin-side down on the grill and leave it alone for 5 to 6 minutes until the skin is crisp and releases easily. Turn carefully and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more until the flesh is just opaque, or until a thermometer reads 50 to 55 °C (125 to 130 °F) in the centre for medium.
Grill the asparagus beside the fish, turning now and then, for 4 to 6 minutes until tender with charred edges.
Rest the salmon for 2 minutes, then serve with the asparagus and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

title: Miso Glazed Black Cod
intro: Buttery black cod cured for two days in a sweet white miso marinade, then baked and blistered until the glaze caramelises.
ingredients: 4 black cod (sablefish) fillets, skin on, about 170 g (6 oz) each
Pickled ginger and steamed rice, to serve
steps: Bring the mirin and sake to the boil in a small pan and let them bubble for 20 to 30 seconds to cook off the alcohol. Turn the heat to low, whisk in the miso until smooth, then add the sugar and stir until it dissolves. Cool completely.
Pat the fish dry and coat every surface with the cooled marinade in a lidded container or a sealed bag. Refrigerate for 24 to 48 hours.

Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F, fan 180 °C) and line a baking tray with lightly oiled foil. Lift the fillets out and wipe off the excess marinade with your fingers or kitchen paper, but do not rinse them. Lay them skin-side down on the tray.

Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the flesh is just opaque and flakes when pressed. Then slide the tray under a hot grill (broiler) for 2 to 3 minutes until the surface blisters with dark caramel spots. Alternatively, cook the fillets entirely under a medium grill for 3 to 4 minutes a side, watching closely because the sugar burns quickly.
Serve straight away with steamed rice and a little pickled ginger.

title: Whole Steamed Fish with Ginger and Scallions
intro: A whole fish steamed until just tender, dressed with seasoned soy and finished with sizzling hot oil poured over ginger and spring onion.
ingredients: 1 whole sea bass or sea bream, about 700 g (1½ lb), scaled and gutted
5 cm (2 in) piece fresh ginger, half sliced, half cut into fine matchsticks
4 spring onions, 2 cut into 5 cm lengths, 2 shredded finely
steps: Rinse the fish, pat it dry and cut two or three diagonal slashes on each side so it cooks evenly. Season lightly inside and out with salt. Lay it on a heatproof plate that fits inside your steamer, with the ginger slices and spring onion lengths under and inside the fish.

Bring a few centimetres of water to a rolling boil in a wok fitted with a rack, or in a large steamer. Set the plate inside, cover and steam over high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, until the flesh at the thickest part flakes away from the bone and the eye has turned white.
While the fish steams, combine the soy sauce, rice wine, sugar and water in a small pan and warm gently until the sugar dissolves.

Carefully tip the cooking liquid off the plate and discard the softened ginger and onion. Pile the ginger matchsticks and shredded spring onion along the top of the fish and pour over the warm soy mixture.

Heat the oil in a small pan until it shimmers and just starts to smoke, then pour it slowly over the aromatics so they sizzle and release their fragrance. Scatter with coriander and white pepper and serve at once with rice.

title: Baked Cod with Herbs
intro: Flaky cod loins baked over crisp baby potatoes with bursting cherry tomatoes, lemon and a green herb oil.
ingredients: 4 cod loin fillets, about 160 g (5½ oz) each
600 g (1 lb 5 oz) baby potatoes, halved
1 tbsp chopped fresh dill or basil
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F, fan 180 °C). Toss the potatoes with 1½ tablespoons of the oil, the oregano, salt and pepper in a large roasting tin about 30 x 40 cm (12 x 16 in), cut sides down, and roast for 25 minutes until they are turning golden.
Meanwhile, mix the remaining oil with the garlic, lemon zest, parsley and dill. Pat the cod dry and season both sides.
Push the potatoes to the edges of the tin, scatter in the tomatoes and lay the cod in the middle. Spoon the herb oil over the fish and top each piece with a slice or two of lemon.
Return the tin to the oven for 12 to 15 minutes, until the cod is opaque and flakes easily and the tomatoes have started to burst.
Spoon the juices from the tin over the fish and serve straight from the tin with the potatoes and tomatoes.

title: Tomato Basil Soup
intro: A smooth, bright red soup of slow-simmered plum tomatoes blended with a big handful of fresh basil and a swirl of cream.
ingredients: 2 x 400 g (14 oz) tins whole plum tomatoes
Large bunch fresh basil, about 30 g (1 oz), leaves picked
Extra virgin olive oil, to finish
steps: Warm the oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion and carrot for 8 to 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Tip in the tomatoes with their juice, breaking them up against the side of the pan with a spoon, then add the stock and sugar. Bring to the boil, lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes.
Add most of the basil, keeping a few leaves back, and blend the soup until completely smooth with a stick blender, or in batches in a jug blender.
Return the soup to a low heat, stir in the cream and season well with salt and pepper. Warm through for 2 minutes without letting it boil.
Ladle into bowls and finish each with torn basil leaves and a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.

title: Pumpkin Soup
intro: A velvety orange soup of roasted pumpkin warmed with cumin and nutmeg and finished with cream and toasted seeds.
ingredients: 1.2 kg (2½ lb) pumpkin or butternut squash, peeled, deseeded and cut into 3 cm (1¼ in) chunks
100 ml (scant ½ cup) double cream, plus a little extra to serve
2 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds, to serve
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (400 °F, fan 180 °C). Spread the pumpkin over a large baking tray, toss with 1 tablespoon of the oil, salt and pepper, and roast for 30 minutes until soft and caramelised at the edges.

Meanwhile, warm the remaining oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cumin, coriander, nutmeg and chilli flakes and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the roasted pumpkin and the stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes so the flavours come together.
Blend until smooth with a stick blender or in batches in a jug blender, adding a splash more stock or water if it is thicker than you like.
Stir in the cream, season to taste and reheat gently. Serve with a swirl of cream and a scattering of toasted pumpkin seeds.

title: Mushroom Cream Soup
intro: A silky, deeply savoury soup built on well-browned mushrooms, thyme, white wine and a generous pour of cream.
ingredients: 600 g (1 lb 5 oz) mixed mushrooms such as chestnut and button, sliced
100 ml (scant ½ cup) dry white wine
Chopped chives or parsley, to serve
steps: Melt the butter with the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Fry the mushrooms in two batches for 6 to 8 minutes each, stirring only now and then, until golden and any liquid has cooked away. Keep a small handful aside for the garnish.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Return the mushrooms to the pan, sprinkle over the flour and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 1 minute, then add the stock. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend the soup to the texture you like, either completely smooth or leaving some small pieces of mushroom.
Stir in the cream, season with salt and pepper and warm through gently. Serve topped with the reserved mushrooms and a sprinkle of chives.

title: Minestrone
intro: A hearty Italian vegetable soup thick with cannellini beans, small pasta and greens in a tomato-tinged broth.
ingredients: 150 g (5 oz) green beans, cut into short lengths
400 g (14 oz) tin cannellini or borlotti beans, drained and rinsed
100 g (3½ oz) small pasta such as ditalini or small shells
100 g (3½ oz) spinach or cavolo nero, shredded
Fresh basil leaves and grated hard cheese, to serve
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 10 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the courgette and green beans and cook for 3 minutes. Tip in the tomatoes, stock and oregano, bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the cannellini beans and the pasta and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally so the pasta does not stick, until it is tender.
Add the spinach or cavolo nero and cook for 2 minutes until wilted. Season generously with salt and pepper, adding a splash of water if the soup is thicker than you like.
Ladle into bowls and top with torn basil leaves and a little grated cheese.
